newsitem.title: UK: LME copper falls further in late London.
newsitem.headline: LME copper falls further in late London.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) three months copper was $18 down from the kerb close in late inter-office activity on Tuesday.

It was bid at $2,243 a tonne, down from the kerb close of $2,261 which was $2 down from Monday, by 1900 GMT when Comex closed. Brokers said profit-taking on the close gained momentum, which also saw aluminium prices closed lower.
A smaller than expected rise in LME stocks of 200 tonnes had initially given copper the chance to break higher, traders said.
"There are bigger fish to fry at the moment than copper and aluminium right now," said another, referring to zinc's strength. "Those two may have done enough for now."
The premium of cash to three months copper narrowed by about $20 over the day, ending at around $165/$170.

Aluminium steadily notched lower after inventories rose by a modest 1,750 tonnes, and ended the kerb $16 down at $1,608. Dealers said sentiment was still bullish overall but prices needed to consolidate considering aluminium's overbought status.
